notes:
I wasn't able to write any notes this time. Because of an error on my side, I never got to read a single page.

I asked for six pages at once: the Enduring Word commentary on Jeremiah 14, the Ellicott, Gill, Pulpit Commentary and Matthew Henry pages on biblehub.com, and the Precept Austin Jeremiah 14 page. My code to display them broke, and I hit my tool limit for this turn before I could fix it. So I don't know if the pages loaded, and I haven't seen any of their content.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for every point. Since I haven't read anything, I can't give verse notes. Writing them from memory would break your rules, so I've left everything out rather than guess.

If you ask me to continue, I'll start with those six pages. Then I'll look for:
- **Protestant traditions:** Spurgeon sermons on vv. 7–9 and 22, Wesley's notes, and Reformed and Lutheran teaching on v. 11 ("do not pray for this people") and on false prophets in vv. 13–16.
- **Other views:** NET Bible notes, Bible Odyssey, and Catholic and Orthodox sources such as Haydock or the Church Fathers on New Advent.
